coverage.r1: Long Latin-transliterated stretch ~23:58-1:00:30 (engine wrote Arabic as Latin). Many opaque engine forms (سوالونا, شطار, Halloween=الحلوين?, Gromela, Zahadi, عذرا=زرقا, علي فيكي) read via Amal's echo. Unclear/skipped: 07:21-07:34 سويت with Amal's صرت/سألت guesses (target verb unclear); 15:39 weather 'رجعوا شوفت كتير'; 15:05 date; 32:36 'ما بتجنن'. بسول at 33:08 is the verb بوصل, not the name سول (Seoul). English prompt echoes ('is tiring', 'visited us') are him repeating her cue, not tier 3. 01:46 confusion over who did homework is comprehension, not written.
coverage.r2: Lesson is mostly English meta-talk about the el- rule from ~17:00; long stretches (19:00-36:00, 37:00-60:00) are Arabizi in Latin script. 22:15 'Halloween' is almost certainly the engine for الحلوين (beautiful) - not flagged. 15:39 رجعوا شوفت كتير (weather reply) is garbled - not judged. 10:47 ثلاث->تلات, 30:04 mata'ib->متعب, 08:26 متهمس, 43:24 يدل=يضل are S4 pronunciation, not counted. 31:32 واطي (low) for short was self-fixed to قصيرة before Amal commented - left out. 24:15 قادين/قاديات: Amal gave both as fine. 17:52 'Uh, no. How about food is important' reads as a redirect, not a fix. 07:12 'It takes لا' unclear.

r3_note: The سجاد/سجادة error occurs three times (08:42 let pass, 09:49 recast, 10:05 recast) - D4, D14, D15 are three separate rows. D5/D16: he meant 'brought'; Amal misread it as بعت. D17 may duplicate an agreed tier-0 row for راحت عليها. سول = Seoul (name).

rows.medi_said: I really need the word for motivated.
rows.amal_said: We know, we know motivation حافز أو دافع. ... a good word for motivation motivated is متشجع.
rows.why: He asked for 'motivated'; Amal supplied حافز/دافع and متشجع (didn't-know).
He used شجاع (brave) for 'motivated'; Amal had just said شجاع is brave and recast متشجع.
Talking about yesterday he used present مش + adjective; Amal recast with past كان negated by ما.

rows.medi_said: أنا كنت بهمس. / أنا كنت أهمس.
rows.why: He used a b-verb (bahammas / ahammas) where the participle متحمس is needed; she recast كنت متحمس (sheet: excited | متحمس لَ). His later متهمس is S4.
rows.r3_why: Fix is verb form -> participle, a B15 rule, so grammar not vocab tier 2.

rows.amal_said: What do you mean؟ ما كنت what؟
rows.why: First use: 11+ takes a singular noun (سجادة); she reacted only to the ما, the noun passed. Same error recast later at 09:58 (D14) and 10:11 (D15).
rows.r3_why: Readers matched two different moments; 08:42 is its own let-pass instance, 09:49 is D14.

rows.why: متحمس takes لـ (sheet: 'متحمس لَ'); right after she said إلهم at 09:00 he said إنهم and she recast إلهم.
rows.r3_why: Real: separate slip after her 09:00 model, recast at 09:08.

rows.medi_said: It would be جابت؟ بجيب، جابت.
rows.why: 'I brought' is جبت; he used the she-form جابت and repeated it at 09:29 and 09:42 despite the recast.
She had just fixed جابت -> جبت at 09:28-09:31 ('بجيب، جبت'); he said جابت again for 'I brought' and she let it pass.
rows.r3_why: He meant 'brought' ('If I brought...', 'I didn't sell' at 10:39), so بعت is her misreading, not a vocab fix; the real error is the past form.

rows.why: 11+ takes a singular noun; she recast سجادة.
rows.r3_why: Real recast, distinct from the 08:42 let-pass (D4).

rows.amal_said: يعني بعت أكتر من عشرين سجادة.
rows.why: Right after her 09:58 fix he said سجاد again; she recast سجادة a second time.
rows.r3_why: Repeat slip after the fix, recast again - own row.

rows.amal_said: بعت، أنت بعت. ... No, no, no، بعت. إيش يعني بعت؟
rows.why: He heard/repeated her بعت (sold) as بعد (after); Amal said no no no, بعت.

rows.amal_said: ما؟ They are a group so they didn't. ... ستروا. Yes.
rows.why: He used a singular form for 'they didn't buy'; Amal prompted 'they are a group' and he fixed to شطارو (اشتروا).
He said مواعد (plural-like form) for 'appointment'; she recast موعد (sheet: appointment | Maw3ed | موعد).

rows.amal_said: So from last week ... So we say من الأسبوع الماضي.
rows.why: He joined 'meeting' to 'last week' with no preposition; Amal supplied من.
Noun + adjective both need el- (she just said من الأسبوع الماضي); he dropped it and she moved on.

rows.medi_said: هي كانت متحمسة كتير لما شفت السجادة.
rows.why: Subject is هي; he used the I-form شفت, Amal recast شافت.

rows.medi_said: لما شفت السجادة. ... So one و عشر.
rows.amal_said: So I showed is a different verb.
rows.why: He meant 'I showed' but used شاف (see); she said 'I showed is a different verb' and he switched to فرج (sheet: show | farji | فرجي).
rows.english: when I showed her the rug

rows.why: 'Showed her' needs the object ending on the verb; Amal recast فرجته and confirmed فرجتها.
One rug (he himself said شفت السجادة at 13:19); the collective سجاد passed without comment.
rows.r3_why: Singular vs collective noun is a plural rule (A9), not a new vocab form.

rows.medi_said: You went-- you went to her-- no?
rows.amal_said: No. راحت عليها. It's like she missed out.
rows.why: New expression she taught at 13:55; he read it literally as 'you went to her' and she explained.
rows.r3_why: Real listening misread, tier 0. Merger: may overlap an agreed tier-0 row for راحت عليها at 13:55 - keep only one if so.

rows.why: Target 'young children are fun'; Amal said his بيضحكوا means 'funny'; he then gave بيبسطوا / بيسلوا.

rows.medi_said: So if I wanna say those expensive dresses, it would be هدول
rows.why: He asked for 'those' but used هدول 'these' (he says 'Hadol is these' at 26:50; sheet: those | هدولاك); Amal's صح was about el- placement.
rows.r3_why: Real but let pass; low because Amal accepted and the focus was el-.

rows.medi_said: هدول فساتين، الصغار الـ، الـ غاليين.
rows.amal_said: Where do I put the L? Those expensive dresses.
rows.why: After هدول the noun keeps el-; Amal prompted and he said هدول الفساتين الغاليين -> صح.
Target was plural 'long trips'; Amal repeated 'Long trips' and he pluralised.

rows.medi_said: So, honak is that, right? / And then honak is that?
rows.amal_said: No, hunak is not in this list. Hunak means over there.
rows.why: He used هناك (over there) for the demonstrative 'that'; sheet: 'that (m) | Hadaak | هداك'.
Target was 'young guy'; he said زلمة (man), Amal stressed young, he switched to شب.
'This family' is singular feminine هادي; he said هدول, Amal repeated 'This family', he fixed.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Both sides arrive or reach.
rows.why: He used وصلونا 'reached us' (engine wrote سوالونا) for 'visited us'; Amal said no, that is arrive/reach; he fixed to زارونا. Sheet: 'i visit | Bazoor | بزور'.

rows.amal_said: There's a big table. ... Do I need L here?
rows.why: Indefinite 'a big table' takes no el- on the adjective; Amal asked 'Do I need L here?'.
طاولة is feminine; he said كبير (he had كبيرة at 34:33, may be engine).
باب is masculine; Amal repeated مفتوح and he fixed ('cause it's bab').

rows.medi_said: So el ba-- No. Yeah, el bab.
rows.why: First word of idafa never takes el-: باب الغرفة المفتوح.

rows.amal_said: Where do I put the ال؟ ... the Arabic lesson of Arabic is درس العربي.
rows.why: In the idafa drill she prompted the el- placement; he moved to dars al-arabi; she explained both readings.

rows.medi_said: is sick. Uh, awahi ... I forgot the word for, like, mild sickness.
rows.why: He forgot 'sick' and asked; Amal supplied عيانة (sheet: 'sick | 3ayaan | عيان').

rows.medi_said: walad al, uh, ayan. / So walad al ayan now, the sick boy.
rows.amal_said: So where, where do I put the ال؟ ... No. ... It's not boy the sick. It's the sick boy.
rows.why: Noun + adjective both take el-; he put it only on the adjective like idafa; Amal said no.
No b- after لازم; Amal repeated لازم and he fixed to يدل.
Stay IN his home needs في; Amal prompted 'In his home', he fixed.

rows.medi_said: الـ ولاد الـ أيان، نه، أيانة، right?
rows.why: ولد is masculine so the adjective stays عيان; she told him the -a form is for a girl.

rows.medi_said: الـ ولاد الـ أيان لازم يدل في بيته.
rows.why: He set out to say 'the sick boy' (42:22) and had الولد at 42:57; here ولاد (plural) clashes with singular يدل / بيته / أيان. Could be engine.
rows.english: The sick boy must stay at home.
rows.r3_why: Real but low - possible engine slip.

rows.amal_said: So for feminine nouns, what do we add?
rows.why: Feminine first word of idafa grows -t; she prompted 'what do we add?' and he answered 'the T'.

rows.amal_said: the apple tree. I'm not describing the tree. I'm saying it's the tree of apples.
rows.why: 'The apple tree' is idafa (شجرة التفاح, first word no el-); he built noun+adjective with el- on both.

rows.medi_said: el kunda-- or kundara el Chanel.
rows.why: Feminine كندرة grows -t before the owner; she said 'Kundera-t because...'. Engine writes his repeat as kundara, so whether he fixed it is unclear.

rows.medi_said: Uh, Fehon. ... Is this pointer rule Fehon Hon?
rows.amal_said: ليش فيه هون؟ ... No, they're just هون. طلاب الجامعة هون.
rows.why: 'Are here' needs no verb; فيه means 'there is'; Amal said no, just هون.

rows.amal_said: What's bag؟ Uh, the other word like big bag، backpack ... شنتة سفر.
rows.why: For 'suitcase' he offered جزدان (purse); Amal asked for 'the other word' and then supplied شنتة سفر (sheet: 'suitcase | Shantet safar | شنتة سفر').

rows.amal_said: So why did you put ال؟ هذه. ... يعني شنتة السفر هذه إلي.
rows.right: هادي شنتة السفر / شنتة السفر هذه
rows.why: شنتة سفر is idafa so el- goes on the second word, not شنتة; Amal asked why he put ال and moved هذه after.
He used the MSA stem يصلوا; Amal recast Levantine يوصلوا (sheet: 'i arrive | bawsal | بوصل').
In a chain the owned thing (بيت) comes first; he started with صديقة, she prompted 'House.', he fixed to بيت صديقة خطيبتي.

rows.medi_said: So after هذي and هدول and هناك and,
rows.why: Again listed هناك (over there) as a demonstrative; she queried and he dropped it for هذاك.
Plain present needs b-; she had just said بشوفك and he answered أشوفك. Farewell formula, could be engine.
